label: 911 / emergency communications center
description: A primary or consolidated Public Safety Answering Point / Emergency Communications Center: 911 call-taking on NG911 call-handling equipment, CAD dispatch for police, fire and EMS, the trunked radio system, the logging recorder, alert and warning, and a backup PSAP.

vocabulary.facility: the communications center (the dispatch floor, the equipment room, the radio sites and the backup PSAP)
vocabulary.public: callers and residents of the service area, and the police, fire and EMS units the center dispatches
vocabulary.frontline: call-takers, police and fire dispatchers, floor supervisors, the 911 systems technician, radio technicians

it: 911 call-handling equipment (ANI/ALI display, ACD, NG911 i3 call handling)
ALI database and supplemental device location
NG911 core services via the ESInet (geospatial routing, text-to-911)
computer-aided dispatch (CAD) and mobile data terminals
records management system shared with law enforcement
logging recorder for 911, radio and text
state message switch / NCIC / Nlets (CJIS network)
IPAWS-OPEN alerting (WEA, EAS), mass notification and outdoor sirens
10-digit admin phone lines on the VoIP PBX
fire / EMS station alerting and CAD-to-CAD links
county network, email, EDR and SIEM
ot: P25 trunked radio system (zone controller, tower sites, microwave backhaul)
dispatch radio consoles, conventional mutual-aid channels and gateways
UPS and generator with the transfer switch
backup PSAP and the mobile communications vehicle

roles.name: 911 Director (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Owns center-level command, evacuation to the backup PSAP, overtime and requests to the policy group.

roles.name: Floor Supervisor (Communications Supervisor)
roles.description: Owns moment-to-moment call handling, the switch to manual dispatch with run cards, and talkgroup patches.

roles.name: 911 Systems / Technical Services Manager (Technical Lead)
roles.description: Owns the call-handling equipment, CAD, ALI, mapping and the recorder, and escalation to the 911 service provider and vendors.

roles.name: Radio System Manager / Communications Unit Leader
roles.description: Owns the trunked radio system, consoles, interoperability channels and the ICS 205.

roles.name: Police / Sheriff Liaison (Patrol Commander)
roles.description: Owns the field response, the swatting response posture and BOLO dissemination.

roles.name: Public Information Officer
roles.description: Owns the call-this-10-digit-number message, social media and the press.

outsideParties: the 911 service provider (ESInet / selective router operator)
wireless, wireline and VoIP originating service providers
neighboring PSAPs (alternate routing and mutual aid)
the FCC (Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau)
the CAD, call-handling and radio vendors
police, sheriff, fire and EMS agencies served
mediaChannels: a resident's Facebook post saying 911 is not answering
a police scanner stream with listener comments
a reporter's records request for 911 audio

noiseExamples: a pocket-dial from a caller who cannot be reached back
a resident calling 911 to report a power outage
a CAD map tile that fails to load in one subdivision
a radio check request from a volunteer fire company
a printer jam at the supervisor's desk
pressureExamples: a post saying 911 is down and giving a scammer's phone number to call instead
a reporter asking how long the caller waited before the fire call was answered
a council member demanding to know why calls were rerouted to the next county
a scanner-stream audience accusing dispatch of sending units to the wrong address
a family member on TV saying nobody answered their 911 call
